findings.description: The function's environment block embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key as plaintext values ('access_key'/'secret_key'), committed to source control and visible in Terraform state, plan output, and to any principal with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration. The inline comment acknowledges the secrets are stored in plain text.

findings.issue_category: missing KMS encryption of environment variables
findings.description: No kms_key_arn is specified, so environment variables are protected only by the AWS-managed default Lambda key rather than a customer-managed CMK. This provides no key-policy access control point and no distinct CloudTrail Decrypt audit trail, meaning any caller with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration retrieves the secrets in cleartext.

The function uses runtime nodejs12.x, which is end-of-life in both Node.js upstream and AWS Lambda and no longer receives security patches or runtime updates, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unfixed.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function executes outside any customer VPC with unrestricted internet egress and no security group or NACL controls. Combined with the embedded credentials, a code-execution flaw has an unrestricted outbound path for credential exfiltration or command-and-control traffic.
